agent.name: A2HA
agent.description: Assistant TO the Home Assistant. Runs your house from chat - reads state, calls services, writes automations and scripts - and hands guests a locked-down button pad through a link that expires when you say so. Guests get big buttons and nothing else: no entity names, no free text, no access to the rest of your house.
agent.vibe: assistant TO the Home Assistant, thank you

secrets.name: HA_BASE_URL
secrets.description: How the agent reaches Home Assistant. With Tailscale this is a tailnet address, e.g. http://homeassistant.your-tailnet.ts.net:8123 or http://100.x.y.z:8123 - no public URL needed. Without Tailscale, a public https URL. No trailing slash.

secrets.name: HA_TOKEN
secrets.description: Home Assistant long-lived access token. In HA: profile (bottom left) -> Security -> Long-lived access tokens -> Create token. Use a dedicated admin user so you can revoke it independently.

secrets.name: TS_AUTHKEY
secrets.description: Optional but recommended. Tailscale auth key, so the agent joins your tailnet and Home Assistant never needs a public URL. Generate at https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys - mark it Reusable AND Ephemeral. Leave blank to reach HA over a public URL instead.

secrets.name: TS_HOSTNAME
secrets.description: Optional. Name this agent shows up as in your Tailscale admin console. Defaults to a2ha.

secrets.name: HA_AGENT_ID
secrets.description: Optional. Home Assistant Assist agent id, used only by pad buttons that fire a spoken phrase instead of a service call. Leave blank for HA's default agent.

secrets.name: PUBLIC_BASE_URL
secrets.description: Optional. Overrides the guest link base URL. Normally left blank - the agent derives https://$AGENT_ID.agents.pinata.cloud/pad automatically. Set this only if you have pointed a custom domain at the /pad route.

secrets.name: HA_SSH_KEY
secrets.description: Optional. Enables editing YAML files in /config, and nothing else turns it on. The PRIVATE half of an SSH keypair whose public half is in the authorized_keys of Home Assistant's official "Terminal & SSH" add-on - paste the whole file, newlines and all (base64 of it also works if your secret store dislikes newlines). Leave blank and the agent cannot touch files, which is the safe default. Only set this if Home Assistant is reachable privately, over your tailnet or LAN; an add-on port sits outside Home Assistant's own login.

secrets.name: HA_SSH_HOST
secrets.description: Optional. Host running the Terminal & SSH add-on. Defaults to the host in HA_BASE_URL, which is right unless Home Assistant is behind a reverse proxy on a different address. Only used with HA_SSH_KEY.

secrets.name: HA_SSH_PORT
secrets.description: Optional. Host port the Terminal & SSH add-on's port 22 is mapped to. Defaults to 22. Only used with HA_SSH_KEY.

secrets.name: HA_SSH_USER
secrets.description: Optional. SSH username. Defaults to root, which is what the Terminal & SSH add-on logs in as. Only used with HA_SSH_KEY.

secrets.name: HA_SSH_PASSPHRASE
secrets.description: Optional. Passphrase for HA_SSH_KEY, if you made the key with one. Leave blank for an unencrypted key.

secrets.name: ADMIN_TOKEN
secrets.description: Optional, and NOT needed on Pinata - the gateway already protects the /admin route. Only for self-hosting: a shared secret required to reach the config API from anywhere other than localhost. Without it, the admin port refuses to bind to anything but loopback off-Pinata.

scripts.build: bash workspace/setup.sh && npm ci --omit=dev --prefix workspace && cd workspace/projects/speeddial && npm ci --omit=dev
